lead: Tesla / TSLA - the believers are buying the drop
smaller: D-Wave / QBTS - quantum is the next AI
Ripple / XRP - the lawsuit is over
Robinhood / HOOD - prediction markets for everyone
why_lead: Tesla is where the drawdown and the crowd coincide on this date: the stock is down 34.59% over 20 sessions from $360.56, while CNBC and Business Insider report retail investors sticking with it after an $800 billion wipeout. Fortune's report that Nvidia overtook Tesla as the most-held stock on Robinhood adds a retail-flow signal, and the simple story the crowd repeats is that believers are buying the drop.
why_smaller: D-Wave is the surge leg of the set, up 82.13% over five sessions, with quantum headlines on Nvidia's first Quantum Day and a six-stock buy pitch giving the attention side.
XRP is the one non-equity trade, with the largest single-session move among the majors (+11.32%) and one regulatory story, the SEC dropping its lawsuit, that the crowd repeats.
Robinhood is the platform trade, bouncing 9.97% over five sessions against a 27.74% drawdown over 20, with a prediction-markets launch that retail is reading as a new product.
considered_not_chosen: Nvidia (NVDA): the most-held stock on Robinhood and a retail-bullish GTC reaction, but down 15.59% over 20 sessions, a smaller move than Tesla's, and the GTC headlines conflict on direction, so no direction is claimed.
Palantir (PLTR): Reddit and meme-stock headlines and a 23.17% 20-session drawdown, but the attention is generic and the catalyst set is thinner than Tesla's.

Nuclear small caps (SMR, OKLO, NNE): large five-session moves and AI-power headlines, but the attention evidence is mostly analyst and aggregator pieces and the theme overlaps the AI-capex coverage elsewhere in the report.

Gold and silver: record-run and squeeze headlines, but the move is modest (GLD up 3.79% over 20 sessions) and the attention is central-bank and institutional rather than retail; the silver-squeeze piece has no price for its ticker in the card data.
The bitcoin memecoin debate (Cathie Wood's worthless-memecoin remarks): retail-attention headlines, but BTC is up only 2.54% over 20 sessions and crypto has its own section.
Nebius (NBIS) and Super Micro (SMCI): sharp 20-session drawdowns (-38.48% and -33.44%) but only one analyst or Seeking Alpha note each, too thin for a smaller trade.
Earlier retail selection notes: none exist in the sandbox for strictly earlier dates, so no editorial memory was applied.
